decision: held: neither trial has open full text. 17985810 combines two open-label studies with one double-blind study (n=120) of 270 mg citrus flavonoids + 30 mg tocotrienols for 4-12 weeks without a named primary outcome in the abstract, and the abstract does not name the product as Sytrinol; 25828621 (240 adults, 12 weeks) reports a null primary LDL-C result at lower doses, but the abstract does not confirm the material is Sytrinol. Product identity and regimens cannot be verified from abstracts. OA retry 2026-10-28: Europe PMC's 25828621 link returned a paywalled Nature landing page; 17985810 closed.
summary: 17985810 abstract reports 20-30% lower total cholesterol and 19-27% lower LDL; 25828621 found no LDL-C or hsCRP difference from placebo (all arms fell ~4-5%). The conflicting results, combined with unverifiable identity, keep the record held.

source_receipts.title_fetched: Effect of citrus flavonoids and tocotrienols on serum cholesterol levels in hypercholesterolemic subjects.
A combination of palm oil tocotrienols and citrus peel polymethoxylated flavones does not influence elevated LDL cholesterol and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels.
